title: Soon is playing at St Luke’s Theatre now through November 15.  Press ...
transcript: Who would have thought that a musical about existential dread would feel so comforting? This new musical, soon, by Nick Blaemire, perfectly captures that feeling of helplessness when you feel like everything around you is crumbling and you just wanna retreat into your own shell. It's a feeling that I think all of us have felt at some point, especially with the world the way it is right now. And in the show is exemplified by our main character, Charlie, who would rather stay at home with her pet fish than go out into the outside world. And the tragedy here is that she is someone with big ideas and dreams, but she feels like she can't allow herself to dream them because the world is ending, so what is even the point? And we see this self sabotage play out over and over again, as she refuses to go on vacation with her roommate Steven or get invested in her budding relationship with food delivery driver Jonah. Jonah is played by Oliver Richman, who you may know on here from his song a day series. He is really great here, as is the rest of the cast, which includes Ava Delaney, Mike Millan and Mylinda Hull. Mylinda Hull in particular, I think, really steals every single scene that she is in as Charlie's detached mother. And then you have the score by Nick Blaemire, which is just hauntingly beautiful. There's actually a cast recording out already, Highly recommend checking it out. and it sounds gorgeous in this space. This is actually a brand new theatre in the attic of Saint Luke's on 46th Street. And given that it's such an unconventional space, I was really impressed by just how polished the sound design was. But this will certainly go down as one of my favorite new musicals of the year. I've been describing it to people as like Kimberly Akimbo if you took out a lot of the over the top humor and just really leaned into the existential dread. But I also realize that makes it sound like this is a miserable show to sit through and it's really not. There is still plenty of laughs and also plenty of emotional beats as well. The show is a vivid reminder to not let the fear of the future ruin the now. And it is definitely going to be getting the coveted Broadway Ben must see from me. This is the kind of bold, original musical that I think so many of us crave. And I really think that you will find it just as moving and haunting as I did.
classificationReason: First-hand review of Nick Blaemire's musical at St. Luke's Theatre. Creator shares a positive opinion and specific praise for individual cast members.
